mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above 2% for three consecutive months predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to expectations of tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains >2% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from the 30-day rolling mean during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly UNRATE falls below 6.5% for two consecutive months, it indicates weakening labor market conditions that coincide with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate slower economic growth.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns exceed the 90-day moving average of prior 60-day returns during the trigger period (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sequential decline in both HOUST (industrial production) and GDPC1 (goods orders) by at least 5% in the same month suggests soft demand, which is associated with a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates a rebound.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 < previous and HOUST < previous by >=5% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant versus the 10-day rolling mean (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO rises above 97 for two consecutive months, it signals strengthening supply capacity that is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors price in future capacity expansion.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain negative in 60% of similar expansionary INDPRO events (quantile regression).

mechanism_narrative: An abrupt jump in CPIAUCSL by more than 0.5% in a single month followed by two consecutive months above 233 suggests accelerating inflation, which predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as risk aversion rises.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% in one month and remains >233 for two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with CPIAUCSL changes (Spearman rho < -0.2).

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS exceeds 135,000 for three consecutive months, it reflects strong labor market absorption that coincides with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as equities benefit from employment resilience.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform the 30-day moving average during the trigger (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both HOUST and RSAFS by at least 3% in the same month indicate weakening demand signals, which drive a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates a soft landing.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous and RSAFS < previous by >=3% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly different from the prior 7-day average (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a supply-constrained environment when INDPRO remains below 95 for four consecutive months is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates production bottlenecks.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during such regimes are not consistently outperforming the 50-day rolling mean (quantile regression).
